summary: 74-year-old woman with vascular disease: sudden crampy left-sided abdominal pain followed within hours by bloody diarrhoea; CT shows thickened splenic flexure/descending colon. ACG 2015: CT with IV contrast, supportive care, colonoscopy within 48 h; antibiotics for moderate/severe disease; surgery for peritonitis/gangrene.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Sudden tummy pain followed by bloody diarrhoea
inputs.hpi: Yesterday evening sudden cramping pain in the left side of the abdomen, then urgent loose stools mixed with dark and fresh blood (5 times overnight). Previous stroke, peripheral arterial disease, type 2 diabetes, on clopidogrel. Was dehydrated from a stomach bug last week. No recent travel. No previous bowel problems.

exam.abdomen: Soft, tender in the left upper and lower quadrants, no guarding or peritonism.
exam.other: PR: dark blood mixed with loose stool.

imaging.name: CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast
imaging.result: Segmental wall thickening with thumbprinting of the splenic flexure and descending colon; no pneumatosis, no free gas; mesenteric vessels patent.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Ischaemic colitis (left colon), non-gangrenous
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Non-gangrenous ischaemic colitis of the splenic flexure and descending colon. Supportive care, antibiotics (moderate disease), colonoscopy within 48 h; surgical review if peritonism.

mustRankTopK.note: The mimic of infective colitis, IBD and diverticulitis; managed differently.

mustInclude.note: ACG 2015: early colonoscopy (within 48 h) to confirm the diagnosis.

mustExclude.note: Non-gangrenous ischaemic colitis is managed supportively; an appendicectomy plan is a contraindicated operation. The exam text records "no guarding or peritonism".
mustExclude.knownGapNote: Web computeClinicalPrompts fires "Appendicitis — emergency surgical indication" and adds the full "LAPAROSCOPIC APPENDICECTOMY — OPERATIVE PLAN" whenever examAbdomen contains "guarding" or "rebound" — including negated text ("no guarding") and localised guarding from other causes.
mustExclude.proposedFix: Gate the appendicectomy operative-plan prompt on the confirmed working diagnosis (appendicitis) or imaging, not on the words "guarding"/"rebound"; add negation handling (no/without/absent) to exam() matching.

mustExclude.note: Anticoagulation is not a treatment for non-occlusive colon ischaemia (only for mesenteric venous thrombosis) and worsens bleeding.

guideline.name: ACG clinical guideline — colon ischaemia
guideline.section: Colon ischaemia: CT with IV contrast; colonoscopy within 48 h; antibiotics for moderate or severe disease; surgery for peritonitis, gangrene, perforation
guideline.citation: Brandt LJ, Feuerstadt P, Longstreth GF, Boley SJ. ACG clinical guideline: epidemiology, risk factors, patterns of presentation, diagnosis, and management of colon ischemia (CI). Am J Gastroenterol. 2015;110:18–44.

rationale: Base mimic: bloody diarrhoea with sudden cramping pain in an arteriopath. Tests that ischaemic colitis ranks ahead of infective colitis/IBD and that the plan is supportive rather than anticoagulant-based.

authoring.author: Claude (colorectal/anorectal cluster)
authoring.notes: Expectations need surgeon sign-off (reviewedBy). Citations verified: false until checked against the source.
